about:
Crego Metal Systems, operating as Crego Roofing of New Mexico, has been based in Albuquerque’s North Valley (Los Ranchos de Albuquerque) since its founding in 1980. The company is family‑owned and operated, with Stephen and Brenda Gregg serving as primary contacts. It began as a local installer and manufacturer of metal roofing for both residential and commercial projects.

The firm fabricates cut‑to‑length metal roof panels, flashing, and trim on site using UL‑approved roll‑forming lines. Its product range includes CMS Panel, R Panel, and Standing Seam profiles, along with seamless and box gutters, plaster trims, and plasma‑cut decorative silhouettes. Custom copper work and green‑roof solutions are also offered. Most standard orders are ready for same‑day pickup; larger orders typically ship within three days.

Crego serves homeowners, building owners, and contractors across residential and commercial construction in New Mexico. Its metal roofing and gutter systems are used on houses, office buildings, and retail centers, while its plasma‑cut designs and copper accents appear on custom architectural projects.

The company emphasizes its UL‑approved manufacturing standards and ANSI/SPRI/ES‑1‑tested flashing that exceeds wind‑uplift requirements. A price‑match guarantee and family‑run continuity since 1980 are cited as key differentiators.

name: Crittco Cable & Fiber
old_description: Crittco Cable & Fiber was incorporated in May 2007. It was formed five years prior as a subsidiary of Crittco Construction. Matt Hale founded the company in 2002 with then partner Barry Brawner. Hale spent 20 years in the water and sewer business and Brawner spent 30 in the telecommunications industry. Together they built Crittco…
about:
Crittco Cable & Fiber operates from Jonesboro, Arkansas, where it was founded in 2002 by Matt Hale and Barry Brawner as a subsidiary of Crittco Construction. Hale brought two decades of water and sewer experience, while Brawner contributed 30 years in telecommunications. The company incorporated in May 2007 and is licensed in Arkansas and Tennessee.

The firm functions as a full‑service utility contractor with directional drilling as its cornerstone. It runs six drill rigs ranging from a 7×11 unit for tight urban sites to a 24×40 rig capable of 28‑inch bores, and can pull back single steel or multiple poly pipes. Additional capabilities include copper and fiber‑optic splicing (single and ribbon), plowing, cable pulling and tugging, trenching and excavating with equipment up to a 200‑series excavator, utility locating, aerial fiber and copper placement, duct washing, fiber blowing, and sewer, water, drainage and electric installation. The operation occupies roughly 8,000 square feet of shop space plus storage and a covered wash bay, supported by a fleet of boring rigs, bucket trucks, backhoes, mini excavators, plows, vacuum excavators, bulldozers, and specialized safety gear. Headcount has grown from the original 12 to around 30 employees.

Crittco serves telecommunications carriers such as Ritter Communications and AT&T, municipal utilities including City Water and Light, and commercial construction projects for Hino Motors, Sam’s Wholesale, Greene County Tech School, and Home Depot. It has also performed infrastructure work around new runways at Memphis International Airport and handles private subdivision and municipal projects in the Marion and West Memphis areas.

The company emphasizes a family‑oriented culture, crediting its long‑tenured crew for on‑time performance and diversified project experience. Leadership states that respect for employees, continuous technological evolution, and a commitment to safe, efficient, and environmentally friendly workmanship set the operation apart.

old_description: Their expertise in custom fabrication and value-added services has been a game-changer for our production line. You can tell they know this business inside and out.
about:
Custom Cable Corp., based in Westbury, New York, has operated since 1974. What began as a small Long Island distributor has grown into a global supplier of industrial wire and cable.

The firm stocks more than 15,000 active wire and cable variations, ranging from high-temperature and coaxial cables to multi-conductor and fiber-optic products. In addition to distribution, it provides value-added fabrication services including precision striping, twisting, paralleling, bundling with custom printing, dyeing, and lashing. The shop also builds generator cable assemblies and fiber patch cords for high-current and high-speed data applications. A team whose combined experience exceeds 150 years, with sales professionals averaging 25 years in the industry, supports technical consulting and rapid fulfillment programs such as emergency shipments and just-in-time delivery.

Customers span manufacturing, aerospace, construction, electronics, and energy and utilities sectors. Testimonials cite senior engineers, project managers, procurement leads, and plant supervisors from those industries who rely on Custom Cable for both standard stock and custom assemblies. The company also serves OEMs, contractors, and other distributors.

Custom Cable was founded on the principle of supplying wire and cable by specification rather than description, emphasizing knowledgeable service and long-term relationships. Its stated differentiators include deep inventory, seasoned technical support, and a commitment to compliance with standards such as UL, NEMA, ICEA, MIL, CSA, and VW-1.

about:
Custom Cut & Fab operates from Mandan, North Dakota, where its staff has been active in metal fabrication since 1992. The business began with a focus on HVAC fabrication and the general construction trade, building a reputation for evaluating customer drawings and resolving design challenges before production starts.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication services, including HVAC fittings, galvanized and stainless steel components, and copper countertops. Its primary processes are water jet cutting on a 6‑by‑12‑foot table capable of slicing material up to 7 inches thick and as thin as 0.002 inch, and plasma cutting on a 5‑by‑10‑foot table suited for metal up to 3/16 inch thick. The water jet handles a wide range of materials — stone, marble, granite, plastics, foam, wood, and ceramics — while the plasma table is geared toward HVAC parts and metal art pieces.

The company serves the HVAC, general construction, and metal arts sectors. Customers range from contractors needing a subcontractor for specific fabrication tasks to clients who want a single source to manage a project from initial design through final delivery.

What sets the operation apart is its long‑tenured team and its willingness to review drawings early, identify potential issues, and propose work‑arounds. The firm emphasizes taking a client’s vision and delivering a finished project, whether that means supplying a single fitting or coordinating a full fabrication package.

about:
Custom Works Inc. operates from Naperville, Illinois, where Serbian‑Macedonian couple Stefan and Melanie founded the company to blend Stefan’s carpentry heritage with Melanie’s project‑management expertise. Stefan grew up in a small town in southern Serbia, spending school holidays in his grandfather Stojan’s workshop, while Melanie brought a background in interior design and operations. Together they launched Custom Works as a vehicle for European‑inspired craftsmanship in the Chicago suburbs.

The shop produces custom furniture, cabinetry, built‑ins, vanities, and one‑off wood pieces, and pairs that output with full‑service home remodeling—kitchens, bathrooms, staircases, mudrooms—and outdoor construction such as patios, decks, and custom exterior features. Projects move through a four‑step design‑build process: consultation, design approval, fabrication (with a typical 8‑10‑week lead time), and on‑site installation.

The client base is residential homeowners across the Chicagoland area. Recent work includes a full basement rebuild after flood damage with a custom bar and media wall, a kitchen remodel that opened up the floor plan and added lighting, a sentimental coffee table milled from a family tree stored for a year, a mudroom with integrated storage, and an entertainment wall with custom TV stand and paneling.

The founders frame the business around four stated values—sustainability, tradition, integrity, and quality—describing their approach as the “European way.” All lumber and materials are said to be ethically and responsibly sourced, and the goal is to create pieces that last for generations rather than follow fast‑furniture trends.

name: Cut & Dry Lumber Company
old_description: At Cut & Dry Lumber, our mission is to reduce green waste by giving second life to Albuquerque trees and inspire others to bring the story of our urban forest into homes, shops, and gathering spaces in our community.
about:
Cut & Dry Lumber Company operates an urban sawmill in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The business was launched in 2018 by a family that had spent more than 40 years in the local tree-service industry, during which they consistently diverted tree material from landfills into wood chips and firewood. The sawmill formalized that practice by processing trees removed from the Albuquerque urban forest into usable lumber.

The company produces live-edge slabs typically cut 2 inches thick with the natural edge intact, and offers custom milling, planing, and finishing services on its Wood-Mizer LX 250 band mill (54-inch capacity, 18-foot length), a 24-inch industrial planer, a 16-inch jointer, and a large sander. It also builds made-to-order furnishings such as river tables, bar tops, desks, benches, and charcuterie boards. All lumber is air-dried for up to two years — one year as logs, then six to eight months after milling — to stabilize the wood in the desert climate.

Customers include interior designers, woodworkers, DIY enthusiasts, and anyone seeking custom furniture made from local species. The shop stocks slabs from Ash, Cottonwood, Cypress, Elm, Honey Locust, Juniper, Maple, Mulberry, Pine, Poplar, Russian Olive, and Sycamore, priced between $5 and $22 per board foot. It does not carry kiln-dried, treated, or structural lumber.

The venture was started to expand the tree-recycling culture in New Mexico, turning what would be waste into one-of-a-kind material that preserves a piece of Albuquerque’s urban forest in homes, shops, and gathering spaces.

about:
Des Moines Steel was founded in 1991 by Elmer Kunkel in Des Moines, Iowa. Kunkel opened the business with a commitment to outstanding service, quality products, and reasonable pricing, a philosophy that continues to guide the company today.

The company supplies a range of steel products and provides in-house processing services including cutting, drilling, welding, and custom fabrication of columns and other structural components. Customers can purchase stock material for pickup or order fabricated parts to specification; the facility serves orders of any size, from single pieces for hobbyists to large volumes for industrial manufacturers.

Des Moines Steel serves a diverse customer base that spans construction contractors, manufacturing firms, artists, and individual hobbyists. Large construction companies and global manufacturers source structural steel and fabricated assemblies, while local artists and hobbyists buy smaller quantities for custom projects.

The business was built on Kunkel's founding pledge to deliver reliable service and fair pricing. That commitment is reflected in offerings such as a local delivery program, a price-match policy, and a loyalty program for repeat buyers.

name: Dickson Industries Inc
old_description: Since 1946, the Dickson name has guaranteed integrity, innovation, and a commitment to excellence. Generations of customers have relied on Dickson to deliver on our promise.
about:
Dickson Industries Inc. traces its roots to April 30, 1946, when Allied Manufacturing Co. was founded at 115 SW 8th Street in Des Moines, Iowa. The company began producing cotton stockinette for meat packers and food processors. Arthur D. Dickson, initially hired as a sales engineer, purchased the business in the 1960s and renamed it Dickson Industries, Inc., moving operations to the Interstate Bakery Building at 325 SW 5th Street. Now in its third generation of family ownership, the company is led by President David Dickson, grandson of the founder.

Today Dickson operates a 50,000-square-foot facility in Des Moines with 49 employees and 216 knitting machines, offering complete cut-and-sew operations and in-house embroidery through its Dickson Designs division. The company produces a range of knit fabrics, garments, and textile products, including custom-designed casings, stockinette, medical fabrics, lab and butcher coats, insulated garments, and filtration fabrics. All products are researched, tested, and manufactured to customer specifications, with proprietary information kept confidential.

Dickson serves food processing (DeliKnit elastic netting, RoastKnit, butcher coats), medical (PPE, surgical drapes, orthopedic fabrics, infant caps, lab coats), industrial (DrainKnit filtration covers, geo textiles, protective sleeves), and apparel markets (custom embroidery, freezerwear, hospitality garments). Its customer base spans national and international businesses, with a centralized Midwest location enabling quick delivery across the United States.

Dickson differentiates itself through collaborative custom product development, emergency response capabilities, and a nationwide sales team that provides ongoing consultation.

Jon’s motivation stemmed from a desire to translate his hands‑on mechanical expertise into the renewable sector, while Holly values the independence of business ownership and helping clients build systems that work. name: Drake Plastics Ltd. Co.
old_description: The science behind Drake’s state-of-the-art injection molding operation assures exceptional quality and consistency in molded parts. When critical tolerances and other features are impractical or impossible to achieve with injection molding alone, we can deploy our precision machining capabilities to provide hybrid molded/machined part solutions to meet the specifications required.
about:
Drake Plastics Ltd. Co. is headquartered in Cypress, Texas. The company was founded in March 1996 by Steve Quance, who recognized an opportunity to supply machinable stock shapes in specialty grades of Torlon® PAI polymer after a major supplier discontinued a product needed for the Javelin missile program. Quance, then an Advanced Products Manager at a large stock shapes supplier, invested personally to establish Drake Plastics and fulfill that initial order.

Today, Drake operates what it describes as the world’s largest facility dedicated to processing ultra high-performance polymers. The company extrudes stock shapes — rod, plate, seamless tube, sheet, film, and balls — in Torlon PAI, PEEK, Ryton PPS, AvaSpire PAEK, Ultem PEI, and proprietary Drake PAI grades. It also runs injection molding and precision machining operations, enabling hybrid molded/machined parts when tolerances exceed what molding alone can achieve. Additional in-house services include re-curing, annealing, priming, coating, laser engraving, CT inspection, CMM inspection, and mechanical testing.

Drake serves aerospace, defense, oil and gas, transportation, electrical, and fluid-handling industries. Its customer base includes OEMs, government agencies (such as the Javelin missile program), universities, distributors, and fabricators worldwide. Products are shipped globally from the Cypress facility, with sales offices in Germany, France, and Taiwan providing local support.

The company emphasizes its near-net stock shapes that minimize machining waste, a quality system certified to AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015, and an on-time delivery rate typically above 98%. Its culture of product and process development aims to deliver unique solutions not available elsewhere, a philosophy rooted in the founding mission to produce what no other supplier could or would.

name: Durable Medical Equipment Re-Use Program, State of Maryland
old_description: Maryland's DME program is improving the quality of life for many Maryland residents by providing medical equipment and supports to help them stay mobile, safe, and connected in their homes and communities. Free durable medical equipment is available to Marylanders with any illness, injury, or disability, regardless of age or insurance coverage. All equipment is collected via donation and is sanitized, repaired, and redistributed to locations throughout Maryland for pickup.
about:
The Durable Medical Equipment Re-Use Program operates from a central warehouse in Cheltenham, Maryland, under the Maryland Department of Aging. The program was established by the state to address mobility and safety needs for residents, though a specific founding year is not published. It functions as a statewide government service rather than a private enterprise, with no individual founders named.

The program collects donated durable medical equipment, sanitizes and repairs it, then redistributes it through a network of more than a dozen distribution centers across Maryland. Inventory is divided into two categories: Basic DME — including canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, and toilet safety rails — and Complex DME — including manual and power wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, and mechanical lifts. All equipment is provided at no cost to the recipient.

The service is available to any Maryland resident with an illness, injury, or disability, regardless of age or insurance status.

The program was created to improve quality of life by helping residents stay mobile, safe, and connected in their homes and communities. name: East Jordan Plastics
old_description: It all started four generations ago when Ken and Shirley Diller founded East Jordan Box and Crate Co. to produce wooden greenhouse flats for bedding plant growers in the Midwest. From those wooden flats to today’s comprehensive line of sustainable plastic plant containers, East Jordan Plastics remains committed to the only industry it has ever served—horticulture.
about:
East Jordan Plastics operates from East Jordan, Michigan, where Ken and Shirley Diller founded East Jordan Box and Crate Co. four generations ago to produce wooden greenhouse flats for Midwestern bedding-plant growers. The business remains family-owned and has served the horticulture industry exclusively for nearly 80 years, evolving from wooden flats to a full line of sustainable plastic plant containers.

The company injection-molds a comprehensive range of horticultural containers — SHUTTLE™ hanging baskets, planters and bowls; the patented SHUTTLE POT® STADIUM® pots and trays with squared-off sides for space-saving shipping; SHUTTLE POT® and SHUTTLE TRAY® lines built for quick de-nesting on automated lines; plus trays, carriers, flats, inserts, and precision-engineered plug and propagation trays. A closed-loop recycling program, certified for Post-Consumer Recycled (PCR) content by AM Testing, feeds reclaimed material back into production.

Customers are greenhouse and nursery growers, from large automated operations to smaller propagators. Bradford Greenhouses and Linwell Gardens are cited as users; the STADIUM line is noted to deliver 12–14% more growing space per bench. Trays and carriers are designed for automated destacking, filling, transplanting and transport equipment, while plug trays support both hand-sticking and high-volume seed sowing.

The company says its differentiation comes from a single-industry focus, a closed-loop sustainability model that recycles used containers into new ones, and product designs — such as the STADIUM® line’s flat sides for labeling and offset printing — that address growers’ handling, shipping and marketing needs.

Electrical Equipment LLC has operated from Idaho Falls, Idaho since 1962. The company is owned and led by Brook Jensen, a Licensed Master Electrician with over 30 years of hands-on experience. The company's SAM.gov registration and compliance with federal work-authorization requirements enable it to serve institutional clients directly.

Electrical Equipment LLC emphasizes integrity, safety, and documentation. Every job follows a mandatory test-before-touch protocol, arc-flash PPE requirements, and a written lockout/tagout program aligned with NFPA 70E. The firm commits to a two-hour emergency response for critical outages, provides before-and-after photos with test readings and written completion reports, and carries $1 million in general liability insurance and $1 million in bonding. All projects are managed through professional software for real-time scheduling, digital invoicing, and complete job history.

Elevate also operates a take-back program with the Compost Stewardship Institute to collect and compost used packaging.

Customers span natural and organic food brands, institutional food service, coffee and tea roasters, cannabis producers, apparel and body-care companies, e-commerce retailers, and restaurants. The company serves businesses of all sizes seeking to replace petroleum-based plastics with certified compostable alternatives.

Elevate was founded on the mission “Eliminate Plastic Waste and Create a Healthy Planet.” The company positions itself as environmentalists first, emphasizing that its products meet ASTM D6400 and BPI certification standards, and that its take-back program ensures packaging actually gets composted, closing the loop in a circular economy.

Eller positions the business on an uncompromising standard of craftsmanship: each piece is built to heirloom quality, with meticulous attention to detail and a deliberate, patient process. The founder’s philosophy — "if something is easy to do, it’s not worth doing" — drives a practice that favors the more difficult path when it yields a better result, aiming to create objects that endure across generations.

Encore’s differentiation rests on its B Corp certification, which embeds social and environmental performance into its legal structure, and its core values of integrity, determination, innovation, humility, curiosity, and impact. The company was started to turn brownfields into “brightfields,” leveraging clean energy to revitalize communities and address the climate crisis.

about:
Era Wire Inc. was founded in 1988 by Richard T. Rae in West Haven, Connecticut, initially operating as a wire straightening and cutting service and a dealer of used wire machinery. The family-owned business relocated to its current facility at 19– in West Haven in 1995 following continued growth. After Rae’s passing in 2015, his son Rich Jr. assumed leadership, adding an on-site distribution warehouse and through-feed centerless grinding to create a one-stop shop for ferrous and non-ferrous wire needs.

The company specializes in precision wire straightening and cutting for round, flat, and shaped materials across all tempers and alloys, complemented by heat treating, torsion straightening, and wire forming. Its through-feed centerless grinding service provides an alternative to turning and milling for components requiring tight diameter and surface-finish tolerances. The Quick Wire Program stocks pre-cut 304 spring-tempered stainless steel (including 304V and 316LVM), aluminum, copper, titanium, and high/low carbon steels, offering same-day shipping on stocked items.

Primary markets include the medical device industry, where ERA Wire supplies precision-straightened Bright Diamond Drawn wire for Swiss screw machining, and broader industrial sectors requiring ferrous and non-ferrous wire processing.

Founded on a “customer first” philosophy summarized by the tagline “We give it to you straight,” ERA Wire maintains ISO 9001:2015 certification (since 2004) and adheres to RoHS III, REACH Annex XVII, California Proposition 65, and conflict-minerals (3TG) regulations, ensuring traceable quality and regulatory compliance for every shipment.

Every project is handled turnkey, from initial site survey and electrical load analysis through custom system engineering, permitting, installation, and commissioning. Commercial clients range from small businesses to large-scale real estate developments, with the company highlighting solar carport structures that provide both shade and power generation. Residential and remote off‑grid installations round out the portfolio.

Experienced Solar differentiates itself through a rigorous site‑survey process that evaluates feeder cables, transformer capacity, panel bus‑bar ampacity, and roof or ground conditions before any proposal. The firm promotes direct, ongoing customer access before, during, and after installation, and targets commercial payback periods of three to five years by leveraging federal tax credits, MACRS depreciation, and state gross‑receipts‑tax exemptions.

old_description: Our roots started with our parent company F-Tech (in Saitama Prefecture, Japan) which was established in 1947 as a manufacturer of metal toys.  In 1959, our relationship and initial business with Honda Motor Co., Ltd began as we started manufacturing motorcycle parts, eventually entering into automotive manufacturing as a tier-one supplier for Honda.   To be a global partner with Honda, F-Tech expanded into North America in 1986, building its first plant in Canada.  As the demand for automotive parts increased, it was realized that a plant in Ohio was needed.
about:
F&P America Manufacturing Inc. operates in Troy, Ohio, where it was founded in 1993 as a distribution and assembly facility for its Japanese parent company, F-Tech. F-Tech traces its roots to 1947 in Saitama Prefecture, Japan, where it began as a metal toy manufacturer. In 1959 the company started supplying motorcycle parts to Honda Motor Co., Ltd., later becoming a tier-one automotive supplier. To support Honda’s North American production, F-Tech opened a Canadian plant in 1986 and established the Ohio operation as demand grew.

The company produces pedal assemblies, suspension components, front and rear subframes, and clutch pedals with integrated sensor assemblies. Manufacturing processes include progressive and traditional stamping of rolled steel, traditional and innovative welding, hydroforming of steel tube, painting, and final assembly of sub-assemblies. The Troy facility employs roughly 900 associates and has doubled its building footprint twice, in 1996 and 2001. F&P America is part of a global network of 19 locations under the F-Tech family.

F&P America serves the automotive industry as a tier-one supplier. Its customer base includes Honda, Toyota, and General Motors, providing bolt-in parts ready for direct installation on assembly lines.

The company emphasizes a commitment to excellence through continuous improvement of technology, processes, facilities, and capabilities. It attributes its quality standards to a quality-minded workforce operating in a safe, clean, state-of-the-art environment.

name: FARM Food Processing Accelerator
old_description: To support the growth of the food processing sector, the WMFPA in conjunction with the Community Foundation for Muskegon County (CFMC) and Muskegon Community College put in motion plans to develop the FARM (Food, Agriculture, Research, Manufacturing Center) accelerator and business development center targeted at stage one or two entrepreneurial companies or existing mature ones that are looking for an offsite location for test manufacturing of new products. A State of Michigan infrastructure grant for over $2million that was awarded in 2019 made it possible to take the vision from a plan to reality.
about:
The FARM (Food, Agriculture, Research, Manufacturing Center) accelerator sits on the Muskegon Community College campus in Muskegon, Michigan. Launched by the West Michigan Food Processing Association (WMFPA) with the Community Foundation for Muskegon County and Muskegon Community College—and affiliated with Michigan State University’s food-processing programs—the project secured a $2 million state infrastructure grant in 2019. Construction started in June 2020 and finished in early 2021. The center was built to help stage-one and stage-two food entrepreneurs, plus established companies needing offsite test-manufacturing space.

The facility offers 8,000 square feet of flexible, food-grade suites for commercial fruit and vegetable processing. It meets USDA and FDA standards and includes loading docks, refrigeration and freezer storage, energy-efficient systems, and waste and water handling. Tenants bring their own processing equipment and lease space on flexible terms, graduating to their own plants as they grow. The site also houses the MSU Mobile Processing Lab, a trailer-scale unit used for teaching and career outreach.

FARM serves early-stage food-processing ventures and mature firms seeking pilot-scale production, connecting them with venture capital, student talent from MSU and MCC, and regional kitchen incubators like Kitchen 242 and the Starting Block. Target industries include food processing and agriculture, with a focus on companies planning North American or export expansion. The center also supports workforce development through MSU’s certificate and degree programs. WMFPA designed FARM as a one-stop shop to move innovations from concept to commercialization, strengthen job training, and bolster West Michigan’s food-processing cluster.

about:
FCPS Electric is based in Bryant, Arkansas, and was founded in 1977 by Lorin Fleming. The company remains independently owned and operated from its original location, having grown from a one‑man operation into a full team of factory‑trained, certified technicians serving the entire state and holding licenses in Tennessee, Texas, Alabama, Iowa, Louisiana, and Mississippi.

The firm provides full‑service electrical contracting for industrial and commercial facilities. Its scope covers electrical design‑build, medium‑ and high‑voltage switchgear installation and service, standby and prime‑power generator installation and maintenance, custom power‑distribution panel design and fabrication, power and control cable wiring, petroleum‑industry electrical work for convenience stores, scheduled equipment inspections, emergency troubleshooting, and 24/7 emergency response. Additional capabilities include aerial lift services using bucket trucks, network cabling and security integration (as an authorized integrator for Turing, Axis, and Brivo), automation and controls, and testing and consulting.

FCPS serves a range of sectors including healthcare (University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences), metal processing (Ryerson), water treatment (Conway County Regional Water), and petroleum retail. Its customer base spans industrial plants, commercial buildings, and critical‑infrastructure operators throughout Arkansas and neighboring states.

The company emphasizes factory‑certified expertise, a live‑answer 24/7 phone policy, and long‑term client relationships — some spanning 20‑plus years. Independent ownership allows it to set its own service standards, and a safety‑first culture is cited as non‑negotiable. Being Arkansas‑based, not a national chain, is presented as a deliberate choice to keep accountability local.

Ferric states its differentiation lies in the highest current density in the industry, elimination of bulky discrete components, and up to 74% component count reduction. old_description: Forever Fabrication specializes in custom automotive fabrication for performance vehicles and automotive enthusiasts. Typical work includes custom exhaust systems, turbocharger piping, mounting brackets, and other performance upgrades.
about:
Forever Fabrication is a welding and fabrication shop based in Lake Elmo, Minnesota. Founded in 2017 by Matthew Belz, the business began as a side venture producing metal art and custom automotive components. Belz, who started welding professionally in 2014 while attending Hennepin Technical College, built experience in motorsports fabrication, stainless and aluminum TIG welding, and production manufacturing before launching the company. A catalytic converter protection system developed during a surge in converter theft helped the business grow nationally.

The shop provides precision TIG and MIG welding on stainless steel, aluminum, and mild steel, along with custom fabrication, CAD layout, and fabrication development from sketches or existing parts. It handles small- to medium-batch runs of brackets, fixtures, assemblies, and short-run production parts, and coordinates laser cutting, CNC machining, bending, and powder coating as a single-source solution.

Forever Fabrication serves two main customer groups: industrial clients such as machine shops, product development firms, and equipment manufacturers needing overflow or specialized TIG welding, and automotive enthusiasts seeking custom exhaust systems, turbocharger piping, and mounting brackets. Notable projects include performance exhaust components for the GM Vortec 4200 inline-six platform and a catalytic converter protection system sold nationwide.

The company emphasizes clean, precise welds, fast turnaround, and clear communication. Its in-house developed exhaust parts undergo real-world testing to refine tone and reduce drone using equalizer tubes and Helmholtz-style resonators, reflecting a focus on engineered solutions rather than generic fabrication.

about:
GAMA Electronics was founded in 1990 by John and Irene Golbeck in Woodstock, Illinois, about fifty miles northwest of Chicago. From its inception, the company positioned itself as a full-service electronic products manufacturer serving customers worldwide.

The company designs and manufactures electromechanical and electronic controls, including custom electronic assemblies, switches, control panels, and wireless remote controls. Its Woodstock facility handles both through-hole and surface-mount PCB assembly, mechanical assembly, wire harnessing, and packaging, with production rates ranging from low-volume to high-volume sustained runs. In-house design capabilities span circuit and PCB layout, software development, and mechanical design for sheet metal, injection-molded plastics, graphical overlays, and control panels. Prototyping is performed internally to validate designs before tooling. Global manufacturing alliances supplement U.S. production.

GAMA serves the transportation, industrial equipment, medical, agricultural, and marine markets. In transportation, it produces patented battery disconnect switches and high-volume cruise control switch assemblies for a major U.S. automotive manufacturer. Industrial customers use motor controls, access controls, remote controls, HVAC controls, gymnasium equipment controls, winch and hoist controls, and lighting controls. Medical work includes a line of heat sealers and custom assemblies for X-ray machinery, pharmaceutical dispensing equipment, and patient assist devices. Agricultural applications feature remote control systems, motor control assemblies, and custom control panels.

The company emphasizes a family-oriented workplace culture, stating that happy employees lead to satisfied customers. Its ISO 9001 certification underpins quality assurance, while the combination of a modern U.S. facility and global partnerships aims to deliver competitive pricing and timely delivery. A focus on research and development means the product portfolio reflects both current offerings and engineering capabilities.

GEM serves food manufacturers worldwide, with a focus on fried‑food production. Its customer base includes major processors such as General Foods, Ore‑Ida, Simplot, McCain Foods, and Lamb Weston. Applications span potato processing (French fries), seafood, vegetable, snack‑food, and malting operations.

The company’s operating philosophy centers on three principles: lowest total cost of ownership over a ten‑year horizon, exceptional service with urgent field response, and continuous improvement through design and manufacturing enhancements. CFD expertise that eliminates recirculation zones and heat spots is cited as a key differentiator, along with easy access to critical components for efficient sanitation and changeovers.

old_description: GRK Manufacturing came into being in May of 1988 when Gary R. Kilday and family formed a corporation to purchase the assets of the Manual Arts Furniture Company. Manual Arts – or MAFCO as it was known – had a long history starting in 1915 as the only piano bench maker for the Baldwin Piano Company of downtown Cincinnati. Baldwin was a major provider of pianos in the United States and it turned to two “shop” teachers – manual arts teachers – to be their makers of piano benches. MAFCO provided Baldwin’s benches for almost 50 years.
about:
GRK Manufacturing Co. is based in Hamilton, Ohio. The company was formed in May 1988 when Gary R. Kilday and his family incorporated to acquire the assets of the Manual Arts Furniture Company (MAFCO), a business that began in 1915 as the exclusive piano bench supplier for the Baldwin Piano Company of Cincinnati. MAFCO had held that role for nearly five decades before its sudden closure.

Today GRK operates a woodworking and sewing facility in Hamilton, a location secured in 1992. The shop produces piano benches, piano covers, and bench cushions, while the woodworking side turns out doors, retail and grocery store fixtures, mirror frames, and components for agricultural tripods. The company also sources and sells imported piano benches and dollies. The sewing division has expanded from a single part‑time seamstress to three full‑time staff, and the woodworking team continues to take on custom projects across multiple product lines.

Historical customers include the Baldwin Piano Company and the Nutone Company (mirror frames), along with a North Carolina firm that bought solid oak tables. Current music‑industry clients purchase both domestically made and imported benches and dollies.

Diversification into non‑music woodwork allowed the company to survive, and in 2023 former Operations Manager Rob Vicena purchased the assets to continue that trajectory.

Generac differentiates itself as the first to make home standby generators affordable and as the current market leader in that category. The company emphasizes quality, affordable power solutions and has pioneered categories such as residential power washers and purpose-built generator engines.

The MIPS subsidiary provides processor IP and virtual platforms for software-to-silicon development.

The company emphasizes differentiation through deep co-innovation with customers, governments, and universities, combining R&D, IP, design, and manufacturing across a flexible global footprint. Its stated mission is to deliver trusted, essential chips that enable AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world, with a quality philosophy targeting zero excursions and zero defects.

Golden Barrel emphasizes its nearly 90-year heritage, family craftsmanship, and commitment to pure, natural ingredients. The business is certified by WBENC as a women's business enterprise and offers kosher-certified products, while maintaining community partnerships throughout Lancaster County.

name: Grace Technologies
old_description: Our GracePort and Grace Permanent Electrical Safety Devices (PESDs) drive innovation, enhance productivity and keep people safe and assets secure through simple and affordable solutions. Our GraceSense Predictive Maintenance System offers predictive maintenance capabilities and provide continuous monitoring and alert personnel when an unplanned shutdown is about to occur.
about:
Grace Technologies is headquartered in Davenport, Iowa. The company traces its roots to 1993 when founder Phil Allen, then a startup system integrator called Grace Engineering, encountered a hazardous electrical safety issue during a friction welder retrofit at John Deere. The solution he devised—a panel interface connector branded GracePort—launched the business, which later became Grace Engineered Products and, in 2020, Grace Technologies.

Today Grace manufactures three core product lines: GracePort panel interface connectors that provide thru-door access to PLCs and control panels; GracePESDs, permanent electrical safety devices that combine presence-of-voltage LED indication with absence-of-voltage test points for lockout/tagout; and the GraceSense predictive maintenance system, a line of IIoT smart sensors that continuously monitor vibration and temperature on switchgear, transformers, and rotating equipment. The catalog encompasses roughly 16,000 SKUs, and the company ships orders worldwide within two to three business days through a distribution network spanning more than 60 countries.

Customers include power plants, food and beverage facilities, chiller plants, and any operation that relies on evaporative cooling towers, as well as broader industrial facilities seeking to reduce incident energy exposure and unplanned downtime. The company’s predictive maintenance webinar series, co-hosted with Infinite Cooling, targets managers of those specific asset types.

Grace says its differentiation rests on four pillars: thought leadership from a team of forward‑thinking engineers; mass customization enabled by its deep SKU count; fast delivery via the 2‑3‑day global shipping promise; and a founding principle of being easy to do business with. Its stated mission is to pursue practical ways of keeping live voltage away from workers before, during, and after maintenance tasks, while empowering maintenance programs with IIoT sensor data.

about:
Grado Creations is based in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and traces its origins to 1998 when master craftsman Jose Grado began building custom furniture and cabinetry with a Southwest aesthetic. The workshop initially focused on hand-carved wood pieces, bespoke kitchen cabinets, and one-of-a-kind furniture for homes and retailers across the United States.

Today the company has pivoted entirely to premium made-to-order home textiles. Its product line includes all-season quilted bedding sets, reversible water-resistant sofa slipcovers, absorbent area rugs and floor mats, and seasonal accents such as quilted tree skirts and laundry organizers. Production uses advanced direct-to-textile dye technology on high-density microfiber and poly-cotton blends, with multi-layer quilting, hypoallergenic batting, and reinforced perimeter stitching. Every item is printed, cut, and sewn individually after an order is placed, avoiding warehouse overstock.

The brand serves the home decor and lifestyle market, targeting consumers who want rustic, Southwestern-inspired textiles that withstand daily use by pets and children. Its direct-to-consumer channel ships nationwide, and the product assortment — exemplified by pet-proof sofa covers, machine-washable quilts, and cabin-themed bedding — is designed for practical, lived-in spaces.

Grado Creations says its differentiation lies in four pillars: authentic heritage-inspired designs rooted in Southwestern and lodge aesthetics; engineering for real-life durability (water-resistant, non-slip, machine-washable); a conscious made-to-order model that reduces textile waste; and transparent, US-based customer support with free shipping on orders over $150 and a 30-day return window.
